evidence.title: A controlled study of remote software development output
evidence.snippet: In a 2023 controlled study, remote developers committed 8% more code per week than their in-office peers, though the authors caution that commit volume is a weak proxy for value delivered.
evidence.sub_question: What does controlled research say about remote work and developer output?

evidence.title: Developer Survey 2024: working arrangements
evidence.snippet: Self-reported productivity rose for 62% of surveyed remote developers, while 21% reported a decline concentrated among engineers with under two years of experience.
evidence.sub_question: What does controlled research say about remote work and developer output?

evidence.title: Effects of remote work on collaboration networks
evidence.snippet: Telemetry covering 61,000 employees showed collaboration networks became more siloed after the shift to remote work, with fewer bridging ties between teams.
evidence.sub_question: How does remote work affect collaboration and code review latency?

evidence.title: Code review latency in distributed teams
evidence.snippet: Median code review turnaround increased from 6 hours to 11 hours in distributed teams, with the largest increases spanning time zones more than four hours apart.
evidence.sub_question: How does remote work affect collaboration and code review latency?

evidence.title: Follow-up: review latency and team distribution
evidence.snippet: A follow-up analysis confirmed the 6-to-11-hour median shift and attributed roughly half of the increase to reviewer availability windows rather than reviewer effort.
evidence.sub_question: What do large-scale industry telemetry studies report?

evidence.title: Meta-analysis of remote work productivity findings
evidence.snippet: Across 14 studies the pooled effect on productivity was small and not statistically distinguishable from zero, and heterogeneity between studies was high.
evidence.sub_question: What do large-scale industry telemetry studies report?

evidence.title: Onboarding outcomes for remote engineering hires
evidence.snippet: Remote hires reached their first independent production change 3 weeks later on average than in-office hires at the same companies.
evidence.sub_question: Where do the findings disagree, and why?

# Remote Work and Developer Productivity

## Measured Output

- A 2023 controlled study found remote developers committed 8% more code per week than their in-office peers. [1]
- Self-reported productivity rose for 62% of surveyed remote developers. [2]

## Sources

1. [A controlled study of remote software development output](https://example.org/controlled-study-2023)
2. [Developer Survey 2024: working arrangements](https://example.org/developer-survey-2024)
